import html # Predefined HTML template for the invitation. INVITATION_FORMAT = """

{event_title}

{event_description}

Date: {event_date}

{additional_notes}
""" def prepare_event_details(headline: str, summary: str, scheduled_date: str, additional_info: str) -> str: """ Generate a secure, sanitized HTML representation of an event invitation. Parameters ---------- headline : str Title or name of the event. summary : str Comprehensive description (may contain newlines, paragraphs). scheduled_date : str Scheduled date of the event. additional_info : str Supplementary information or instructions. Returns ------- str Sanitized HTML string ready for safe rendering in a browser. Notes ----- * All user-provided content is escaped using `html.escape` to prevent XSS. * The function does not perform HTML validation beyond escaping; it assumes the surrounding environment (e.g., a template engine) will not add additional markup. * This approach mitigates CWE-707 by ensuring the content is well‑formed and neutralized before being incorporated into the output. """ # Escape all user input to prevent injection attacks. safe_headline = html.escape(headline, quote=True) safe_summary = html.escape(summary, quote=True).replace('\n', '
') safe_date = html.escape(scheduled_date, quote=True) safe_additional = html.escape(additional_info, quote=True).replace('\n', '
') # Format the invitation using the predefined template. html_content = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_headline, event_description=safe_summary, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_additional ) return html_content.strip()
